perspectives.conclusion: Use one canonical authority manifest for immutable GitHub, host, service, workspace, package, sudo, and protocol facts. The installer and verifier must consume or be mechanically checked against that same authority; UID or runner labels alone do not prove host identity.

PRs 1293 and 1294 are split-brain. The consolidated implementation must fix mixed-generation publication, unbounded privileged input, SUDO_UID fallback, incomplete live ownership verification, cross-job cleanup deletion, and digest drift.

Create one clean consolidation PR from current main, use PR 1294's package/protocol as the implementation base and PR 1293's descriptor-bound verifier/race tests as the security basis, and require offline plus dedicated-runner gates before live authorization.

consensus: Do not merge PR 1293 or PR 1294 as-is.
Deliver one new consolidation PR from current protected main and supersede both old PRs only after the new exact head is independently reviewed and tested.
Keep host installation, runner-group workflow policy mutation, workflow dispatch, merge, and other live mutation outside this consolidation pipeline.
Keep runner group 6 reconciliation-only until a separate guarded rollout proves the installed contract and authorizes exact workflows.
Treat the absent group-7 protected runner as a real validation blocker, never as permission to bypass or substitute group 6.
